stem: The Group 14 elements show a change from non-metallic to metallic character down the group.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Table 3.1 shows some properties of two Group 14 elements, $\text{C}$ and $\text{Sn}$, in their standard states. The table is incomplete.

Table 3.1

|  | $\text{C}$ (graphite) | $\text{Sn}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| state and appearance in standard state | grey shiny solid | silvery solid |
| electrical conductivity |  | good |
| type of bonding |  | metallic |
| type of structure | giant |  |

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Identify the lattice structure shown by graphite.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why $\text{Sn}$ has good electrical conductivity.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Carbon is found in inorganic compounds such as carbonates.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of magnesium carbonate with dilute $\text{HCl}\text{(aq)}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Describe the thermal stability of the carbonates down Group 2.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Ammonium carbonate undergoes an acid-base reaction with $\text{NaOH}\text{(aq)}$.

Explain this statement.

parts.label: (c)
(c)(i)
parts.text: Complete the graph in Fig. 3.1 to show the third to sixth ionisation energies of $\text{Si}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Construct an equation to represent the second ionisation energy of $\text{Si}$.

parts.label: (d)
(d)(i)
parts.text: Explain the trend in the boiling points of the Group 14 hydrides shown in Fig. 3.2.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Deduce the shape of a molecule of $\text{SiH}_4$.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: Silicon readily reacts with elements of high electronegativity.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation for the formation of $\text{SiCl}_4$ from its constituent elements.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Describe what is observed when a small sample of $\text{SiCl}_4$ is added to water.

parts.label: (e)(iii)
parts.text:
$\text{SiO}_2$ is a white solid that melts above $1700^{\circ}\text{C}$.

$\text{SiCl}_4$ is a colourless liquid at room temperature.

Explain the difference in the melting points of these two compounds with reference to their structure and bonding.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
Tin forms an amphoteric oxide, $\text{SnO}_2$.

Suggest the formula of the tin compound that forms when $\text{SnO}_2$ reacts with $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in an acid-base reaction.
